incident_summary: Customers experienced double charges, pending orders, and payment timeouts. 44 of 1580 orders had duplicate successful charges, with 13 occurring before the v2.14.0 deployment that changed timeout settings.
missing_information: Exact logs showing idempotency key usage per retry request
Complete provider latency data during the 12:00‑15:00 window on 2026‑10‑12
Correlation of individual timeout events with specific duplicate‑charge orders

recommended_actions.description: Collect detailed request logs to verify whether idempotency keys were sent on each retry and map timeouts to specific orders.
Update the payment retry logic to always include the original idempotency key, preventing duplicate charges on retries.

recommended_actions.note: escalated: the description mentions a destructive step
recommended_actions.description: Work with the payment provider to confirm duplicate charges and process refunds for affected customers.

root_cause_hypothesis.title: Missing idempotency key on payment retries
root_cause_hypothesis.explanation: All duplicate-charge orders retried without an idempotency key, allowing the provider to process a second charge when the first attempt timed out. This explains the double charges and many pending orders where the second charge succeeded but the order state was not updated.

alternatives.title: Deployment v2.14.0 reduced client timeout, increasing timeout‑related retries
Provider latency spikes caused timeouts and subsequent retries

unexplained_by_top_hypothesis: None; the evidence fully supports this mechanism.
